title: The Lord's care for the meek and obedient virgin
english: Do everything for the Lord, and do not seek praise from people, because human praise is like a flower of the grass, but the praise of the Lord endures forever. The Lord loves a gentle virgin, but a quick-tempered virgin will be hated. A virgin who obeys will receive mercy, but one who talks back is utterly foolish. The Lord will destroy a grumbling virgin, but he will rescue a thankful one from death. Shameful laughter and shamelessness are disgraceful, and every fool gets tangled up in such things. A woman who adorns her clothes will end up outside modesty as well. Do not live with worldly women, so that they do not twist your heart and make your righteous plans worthless. Plead with the Lord in tears at night, and let no one notice that you are praying, and you will find grace. The desire for wanderings and the longing for other people's houses overturns the settled state of the soul and corrupts its eagerness. A faithful virgin will not be afraid, but an unfaithful one will flee even from her own shadow. Envy melts the soul, and jealousy eats it up. A woman who despises her weak sister will be far from Christ as well. Do not say, "This is mine and that is yours," for in Christ Jesus all things are shared. Do not meddle in another person's life, and do not gloat over your sister's fall. Give aid to virgins in need, and do not boast about your noble birth. Do not speak up with a word from your mouth in the assembly of the Lord, and do not let your eyes roam. For the Lord knows your heart, and he watches all your thoughts.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Evagrius continues his series of counsels to the consecrated virgin, warning her against anger, luxury, gossip, and worldly distractions, and urging her to seek only the Lord's approval.

title: Guarding the virgin's soul from desire, sorrow, and defilement
english: Push away every evil desire from yourself, and your enemies will not grieve you.
Sing from your heart, and do not merely move your tongue in your mouth.
A foolish virgin will love silver, but the prudent one will add even her own morsel of bread.
As a rush of fire is hard to quench, so the soul of a wounded virgin is hard to heal.
Do not hand your soul over to wicked thoughts, lest they defile your heart and drive pure prayer far from you.
Heavy grief and unbearable spiritual apathy—but tears poured out to God are stronger than both.
Hunger and thirst wither evil desires, and a good vigil purifies the mind.
Love turns away anger and rage, and gifts overturn resentment.
The one who secretly slanders her sister will be thrust out of the bridal chamber, and she will cry out at its doors, and there will be no one to answer.
The lamp of a merciless virgin will be quenched, and she will not see her bridegroom when he comes forth.
Glass struck by a stone will be shattered, and a virgin who touches a man will not be held guiltless.
A gentle woman is better than an angry and wrathful virgin.
The one who draws out a man's words with laughter is like one who fastens a noose around her own neck.
As a pearl in a golden setting, so is a virgin veiled by modesty.
Songs of demons and flutes weaken the soul and destroy its vigor; guard this at all times, lest you become a reproach.
Do not delight in jokes, and do not rejoice with those who mock, for the Lord has abandoned them.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Evagrius continues his series of short counsels to the consecrated virgin, warning her against desires, evil thoughts, and the dangers that can quench her lamp and bar her from the bridal chamber.

title: Do not judge and the reward of a pure virgin
english: Do not despise your sister when she eats, and do not become proud of your own self-control. You do not know what the Lord has decided or who will stand before him. She who feels pity for her bruised eyes and her wasting flesh will take no delight in freedom from passion in her soul. Self-control is a heavy burden and purity is hard to achieve, yet nothing is sweeter than the heavenly bridegroom.

The souls of virgins will be filled with light, but the souls of the impure will gaze on darkness. I have watched men corrupt virgins with false doctrines and make their virginity worthless. So listen, child, to the doctrines of the Church of the Lord, and let no stranger persuade you away from them. The righteous will inherit light, while the godless will dwell in darkness.

Virgin eyes will see the Lord. Virgin ears will hear his words. A virgin mouth will kiss her bridegroom. A virgin sense of smell will hasten after the fragrance of his ointments. Virgin hands will touch the Lord, and purity of flesh will be accepted. A virgin soul will be crowned and will live with her bridegroom forever.

She will receive a spiritual garment and will feast with the angels in heaven. She will kindle a lamp that cannot be quenched, and the oil in her jars will never fail (Matthew 25:4). She will obtain eternal wealth and will inherit the kingdom of God. Child, my words have now been spoken to you, so let your heart keep what I have said. Remember Christ, who guards you, and never forget the worshipful Trinity.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Evagrius closes his counsels to the virgin by contrasting pure and impure souls and charging her to keep his words and remember Christ and the Trinity.
